comment: How a path in the ByteRipper (macOS) repository maps onto this one.
`modules` is matched by longest path prefix; `notApplicable` is checked
first and removes a path from the report entirely. `status` says how far
the port has got: planned | in-progress | ported.
Keeping this file honest is the whole point of the skill — an unmapped
path is reported as unmapped rather than silently ignored.

notApplicable.why: Window and tab management: one workspace per browser tab (D11).
Window and tab management: one workspace per browser tab (D11).
Window and tab management: one workspace per browser tab (D11).
A browser cannot know a file is open in another tab.
File-type registration needs an installed PWA; out of scope.
Pane dragging between tabs is replaced by explicit commands.
AppKit split view; the web uses CSS grid with a resizer.
AppKit-side tool-module contract; the web has its own.

modules.note: Storage, piece table, diff, search, segments, undo, decoding. The heart of the port. Ported as of M4: the storage and document files, the text and selection files, UndoHistory, DiffEngine with DiffBlock and DiffHunkIndex, and ClipboardCodec (as text/hexText.ts) — each with its upstream tests. StorageSaver does not port as a file: its POSIX strategies become src/platform/files/fileSink.ts, where the browser supplies the atomicity. Still planned: SearchEngine and SmartSearch (M5), SegmentWriter and SegmentReplacer (M7), PatternLibrary (M11), ContentSnapshot and TemporaryFileStore with Duplicate (M7).
The shared UEFI image parser. Ported wholesale; the lazy-tree contract is the part to preserve exactly.
ME/CSME analysis. Crypto/RSA.swift and Decompress/Huffman.swift are the two compute-bound spots kept behind a narrow interface.
The bridge between the document's bytes and the parser's ByteSource.
Colours. A change here is usually a CSS-variable change there.
Pure target ports to the tool's model; the UI target is rewritten as React.
Check on each change whether this is still the right counterpart.

Behaviour ports, drawing does not: AppKit drawRect becomes a canvas renderer with a glyph atlas. Ported as of M2: HexLayout (whole, with its tests), WordSize, and the byte-significance and address-split rules out of HexTheme. HexView's 3.5k lines are split between src/render/hexGrid (drawing) and src/ui/pane (events); its editing, caret-nibble and difference paths wait on M3 and M4.

PaneViewModel's editing half is src/core/edit/typingController.ts — a state machine with a dozen rules, kept out of the component so it can be tested without a DOM. Its view half is src/ui/pane/HexPane.tsx. Segments, bookmarks and the tool panel wait for M7 and M8.
File access diverges hardest here: security-scoped bookmarks become IndexedDB handles. src/platform/files carries the capability detection and the open and drop paths as of M2; the save path is M4.
File drops port; pane drags do not.
Menu commands become the toolbar and the command palette.
A new design document upstream usually means a decision this project has to take a position on.
Data-refresh skills (GUIDs, NVRAM types, ME databases) have counterparts here, driven by CI rather than by hand.
A feature described upstream is a feature to decide about here.
The app-level flow tests. Their web counterpart is the end-to-end suite; a changed flow test upstream usually marks a behaviour change worth porting even when the production diff looks cosmetic.
Drives the comparison: starts a scan, cancels a superseded one, applies an edit incrementally. The actor becomes a worker with a hand-written protocol (D5).
The two-pane layout, side by side and stacked. The AppKit split view does not port (see Packages/ALSplitView); the web uses CSS grid, and the resizer is still to come.
Bookmarks and recents in the empty state arrive with M7 and M11.
Transient notices — a wrapped search, a refused paste — land in the status bar here.
